get.description:
Customizations tied to no model and no user, so usable with any model.

Every entry carries its `path`: the names from the root of the tree down to itself.
The optional `path` query filters that tree like a directory listing, case-insensitively.
`*` matches within one segment, `**` spans any number of them, and a trailing `/` is
shorthand for `/**`.

Given this tree:

    ROOT
    └── PARENT
        ├── CHILD 1
        └── CHILD 2

these are the possible filters:

    path             returns
    ---------------  --------------------------------------------
    (omitted)        everything, flat
    ROOT/PARENT      that node only
    ROOT/PARENT/*    its direct children
    ROOT/PARENT/**   its whole subtree, without PARENT itself
    ROOT/PARENT/     same as ROOT/PARENT/**
    ROOT/**          PARENT and both children
    **/PARENT        that node wherever it sits in the tree
    **/CHILD *       both children, at any depth
    *                roots only, so ROOT

The pattern always spans the whole path, so a bare `PARENT` means "a root called
PARENT" and matches nothing here. Prefix it with `**/` to search by name instead.

Every other character is a literal, so a customization called `v1.4` or `a?b`
needs no escaping. Globs longer than 200 characters are rejected.

parameters.description: Directory-style glob over the full path. See the description above.

anywhere.summary: By name pattern, at any depth

delete.description: Deletes the listed jobs, which must all belong to the caller. The batch is all-or-nothing: an unknown ID returns 404 and a foreign ID returns 403, in both cases without deleting anything. Deletion mode follows the account preference: by default the jobs are soft deleted and their masks removed, while an account with permanent removal enabled has the job data stripped irreversibly. Cached results are invalidated either way.
